questions.question: Diwan-i-Am, containing the marble canopy ornamented with beautiful panels of pietra dura work, is a part of which monument?
questions.solution:
• Diwan-i-Am (Hall of Public Audience) is part of the Red Fort in Delhi.
  • It was used by Mughal emperors for public meetings.
  • Pietra dura is an Italian term for inlaying cut, polished, colored stones into marble or other hard surfaces.

questions.question: Which red and buff sandstone is the tallest tower in India built in the thirteenth century?
questions.solution:
• Qutub Minar (Delhi) is the tallest tower in India built in the thirteenth century.
  • It has a diameter of 14.32 m at the base and about 2.75 m at the top, with a height of 72.5 m.
  • Qutb-ud-Din Aibak laid the foundation of the Minar in AD 1199.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about temples of Khajuraho?
a) Equal importance is given to human experience and spiritual pursuit.
b) Jain and Hindu temples are also found at Khajuraho.
c) Chausanth Yogini temple is one of the important temples here.
questions.solution:
• All statements a, b, and c are correct.
  • Khajuraho's temples are known for their extensive erotic sculptures and highly stylised features.
  • Equal importance is given to human experience and spiritual pursuit.
  • Both Jain and Hindu temples are found at Khajuraho.
  • Chausanth Yogini temple is one of the important temples here.
  • Notable examples include the Kandariya Mahadeo temple (dedicated to Lord Shiva) and the Lakshmana temple (dedicated to Vishnu).

questions.question: The title of Chief of the Merchants' or 'Malikut-Tujiar' was conferred on Mahmud Gawan by which of the following Bahamani kings?
questions.solution:
• Humayun Shah conferred the title 'Malik-ut-Tujiar' (Chief of Merchants) on Mahmud Gawan.
  • Mahmud Gawan (Khawaja Mahmud Gilani) was a Persian trader who rose to prominence in the Bahmani kingdom.
  • He was appointed as Prime Minister with complete control over military affairs.

questions.question:
Match the following books with their respective authors:
a) Tajul Ma'asir → i) Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi
b) Khazain-ul Futuh → ii) Hasan Nizami
c) Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi → iii) Ziauddin Barani
d) Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi → iv) Amir Khusrav
questions.solution:
• The correct matching is:
    • Tajul Ma'asir → Hasan Nizami
    • Khazain-ul Futuh → Amir Khusrav
    • Tarikh-i-Firuzshahi → Ziauddin Barani
    • Tarikh-i-Mubarakshahi → Yahya bin Ahmad Sirhindi
  • Other ancient books and authors: Akbar-Namah - Abul Fazal, Buddhacharita - Ashvaghoshsa, Prithviraj Raso - Chand Bardai, Geet Govinda - Jaidev, Rajtarangini - Kalhana, Kumarasambhavam - Kalidasa, Ashtadhyayi - Panini, Mahabhashya - Patanjali.

questions.question: According to which of the following foreign travellers, people of Delhi used to write letters containing abuses to the Sultan, therefore, in order to punish them, the Sultan decided to shift the capital?
questions.solution:
• Ibn Battuta, a traveler from Morocco, authored Rihla (written in Arabic).
  • He provided rich details about social and cultural life in the subcontinent during the 14th century.
  • According to him, people of Delhi wrote abusive letters to the Sultan, so Muhammad Bin Tughlaq decided to shift the capital.
  • The Sultan appointed Ibn Battuta as the qazi (judge) of Delhi.

questions.question: Chand Bardai's famous literary work ______ mentions Prithviraj Chauhan's love story and heroic deeds.
questions.solution:
• Prithviraj Raso is a Braj language epic poem by Chand Bardai about the life of Prithviraj Chauhan.
  • Other ancient books and authors: Ain-i-Akbari - Abul Fazl, Mahabharata - Vyasa, Ramayana - Valmiki, Shakuntala - Kalidasa, Mudrarakshasa - Vishakhadatta.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the astronomical observatories in North India:
1. Sawai Jaisingh II established five Jantar Mantar observatories at Delhi, Jaipur, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi.
2. Sawai Jaisingh II founded the city of Jaipur on 18 November 1727 AD.
3. He was appointed the Subedar (governor) of Agra in 1722.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• All statements 1, 2, and 3 are correct.
  • Sawai Jaisingh II established five Jantar Mantar observatories in North India.
  • He founded Jaipur on 18 November 1727 AD.
  • He was also appointed the Subedar (governor) of Agra in 1722.

questions.question: Which of the following dynasties' genealogy was found in the Bijolia inscription?
questions.solution:
• The Bijolia inscription reveals the genealogy of the Chahamana (Chauhan) dynasty.
  • It reveals that Chauhans are Vats Gotriya Brahmins.
  • The inscription provides information about Jabalpur, Shakambhari, and Srimal.

questions.question: Who was the founder of the Bahmani Sultanate?
questions.solution:
• Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah founded the Bahmani Sultanate in 1347.
  • Its capital was Ahsanabad (Gulbarga) from 1347 to 1425, later shifted to Muhammadabad (Bidar).

questions.question: Which State was founded by Nizam-ul-Mulk in 1724?
questions.solution:
• Hyderabad was founded by Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah (Chin Qilich Khan) in 1724.
  • He was one of the most powerful members at the court of Mughal Emperor Farrukh Siyar.
  • He was entrusted first with the governorship of Awadh and later given charge of the Deccan.

questions.question: Under the Bahmani kingdom, the provinces were administered by
questions.solution:
• Under the Bahmani kingdom, provinces were administered by Tarafdars.
  • The Bahmani Kingdom (established in 1347 by Ala-ud-din Hassan Bahman Shah) was divided into four administrative regions called 'taraf': Daulatabad, Bidar, Berar, and Gulbarga.
  • Each was governed by a tarafdar or subedar.

questions.question: Which of the following forts was built by Raja Rai Singh in 1588?
questions.solution:
• Junagarh Fort in Bikaner, Rajasthan, was built by Raja Rai Singh in 1588.
  • It was originally called Chintamani and later renamed to mean 'Old Fort'.
  • Amer Fort was built by Raja Man Singh and expanded by Sawai Jai Singh.
  • Kumbhalgarh Fort was constructed by Rana Kumbha in the 15th century.

questions.question: After the breakup of the Bahmani kingdom, how many independent states arose?
questions.solution: • After the death of Muhammad Shah II in 1482, the Bahmani Kingdom disintegrated into five independent states: Bijapur, Ahmednagar, Berar, Golconda, and Bidar.

questions.question: Who among the following Bahmani sultans transferred his capital from Gulbarga to Bidar?
questions.solution:
• Ahmad Shah (1422-1435) transferred the Bahmani capital from Gulbarga to Bidar.
  • The Bahmani Sultanate was established by Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (Zafar Khan) in 1347.
  • The kingdom comprised parts of present-day Karnataka, Maharashtra, and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: Europeans entered India with a mindset of trading only. This streak was initiated by which of the following European nations?
questions.solution:
• The Portuguese were the first Europeans to come to India by sea routes in 1498, led by Vasco da Gama at Calicut (Kerala).
  • European nations arrived in India in this order: Portuguese, Dutch, English, Danish, and French.
  • The Portuguese were also the last to leave India in 1961.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Nawabs of Bengal:
1. Siraj-ud-Daulah succeeded Alivardi Khan as the Nawab of Bengal in 1756.
2. Alivardi Khan ruled Bengal from 1740 to 1756.
3. Mir Qasim was the Nawab of Bengal from 1765 to 1768.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
• Statements 1 and 2 are correct.
  • Siraj-ud-Daulah succeeded Alivardi Khan as the Nawab of Bengal in 1756.
  • Alivardi Khan ruled Bengal from 1740 to 1756 and successfully resisted Maratha invasions.
  • Statement 3 is incorrect: Mir Qasim ruled from 1760 to 1763, not 1765-1768.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT pair of a famous minaret and its construction year in India.
questions.solution:
• The incorrect pair is Char Minar-1664 CE.
  • Char Minar was built by Sultan Mohammed Quli Qutb Shah in 1591 (not 1664) in honour of his wife Bhagmati in Hyderabad.
  • Shaheed Minar was built in memory of Major-General Sir David Ochterlony.

questions.question: What did the term 'bhoga' refer to during the medieval period?
questions.solution:
• 'Bhoga' referred to revenue assignments during the medieval period.
  • Other types of tax: Kara (generic term for taxes), Hiranya (tax on special produce taken in cash), Chat (security tax), Prataya (toll tax).

questions.question: Joseph Francois Dupleix was the Governor General of which of the following East India companies in India?
questions.solution:
• Joseph Francois Dupleix was the Governor General of the French East India Company in India (appointed in 1742).
  • The French were the last Europeans to arrive in India.
  • French East India Company: Established in 1664, first factory in Surat (1668), second in Masulipatam (1669), headquarters in Pondicherry.

questions.question: Rajaram was the leader of which of the following revolts against the Mughals?
questions.solution:
• Rajaram was the leader of the Jat revolt (Mathura) in 1669 CE against Aurangzeb.
  • Satnami revolt (1672): Satnamis (peasants, artisans, untouchables) rebelled against Aurangzeb in Narnaul (Haryana).
  • Bundela Rebellion (1842): Jawahar Singh Bundela of Chandrapur and Madhukar Shah of Narhat were leaders.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Shahnameh' (Book of Kings) was composed by Ferdowsi.
2. Ferdowsi was the court poet of Mahmud of Ghazni.
Which of the statements given above is/are incorrect?
questions.solution:
• Statement 1 is correct: Ferdowsi composed the Shahnameh (Book of Kings).
  • Statement 2 is incorrect: Ferdowsi was not Mahmud of Ghazni's court poet; their patronage relationship was strained and contested.

questions.question: Malik Ambar, who resisted Mughals in Deccan, was an able administrator of which state?
questions.solution: • Malik Ambar was an African-origin statesman and military leader who served as the regent of the Nizam Shahi dynasty in Ahmednagar (now part of Maharashtra).

questions.question: The Imadshahi family was known for the foundation of which state?
questions.solution:
• The Imadshahi family founded the state of Berar (Maharashtra).
  • Imad Shahi Dynasty was established by Fathullah Imad Ul Mulk (1490).
  • He fortified Gavilgad and Narnala.
  • The Berar Sultanate was annexed by Sultan Murtaza Shah of Ahmednagar in 1574. Capital: Ellichpur.

questions.question: In the 15th century, a text called ______ is ascribed popularly to Lochan Kavi.
questions.solution:
• Raag Tarangini is ascribed to Lochan Kavi (Lochan Pandit) from the Mithila region (Bihar).
  • It initiated an alternative system of the division of ragas, 'the Thaat system'.
  • Sangeet Darpan was written by Damodar Pandit.
  • Anup Rag Vilas was written by Kumar Gandharva.
